title: Argo + Helm CI/CD and KMS image rotation playbook (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for CI/CD and release mechanics for private deployments (VPC / on-prem) focusing on: Helm charts + Argo GitOps flows, image signing & verification (cosign / KMS), terraform module notes for KMS/registry wiring, and a safe image/key rotation + canary upgrade pattern. Draft: not final; contains TODOs and decisions to surface.

Scope & assumptions:
- Applies to private deployments managed via Argo CD (GitOps repo per-cluster or per-tenant) and Helm charts templated in the gitops repo.
- Registry used: customer-managed private registry (ECR / GCR / Harbor) with image signing enabled.
- KMS: customer KMS (AWS KMS or HSM) used for signing keys; Redwood operators have minimal privileges described in infra modules.
- Terraform modules are used by infra teams to provision KMS keys, IAM bindings, and registry lifecycle.
- CI runs in Redwood CI (or customer CI); build artifacts pushed to registry, signed, and then image tag written to gitops repo to trigger Argo sync.

High-level flow (happy path):
1) Build pipeline (CI): build image -> run unit/integration tests -> produce semver+sha tag (e.g., 2025.11.04-rc1+sha1234).
2) Sign artifact: cosign sign --key kms://projects/.. - produces signature blob stored in registry and OCI attestation.
3) Push image to registry (immutable tag).
4) CI opens PR updating apps/<app>/values.yaml with new image tag (or Chart.lock), linking to release notes + signed digest.
5) GitOps repo PR triggers PR checks (policy: image signature verification, allowed-registries).
6) Merge PR -> Argo CD auto-sync (or manual promote depending on policy) -> Pre-sync hooks execute canary manifests.
7) Canary verification: run smoke tests (k8s probes, synthetic requests via service mesh), wait N minutes, check metrics (latency, error rates).
8) Promote to full release or rollback to previous pinned image if thresholds exceeded.

Key design decisions (to validate with security / customers):
- Who holds signing keys? Preferred: customer KMS with Redwood-managed signing principal. Alternative: customer rotates keys and grants a signing role to Redwood service account.
- Use cosign + sigstore attestation vs in-house signing. Recommend cosign for ecosystem compatibility.
- Admission controller: cluster-level image signature verification (admission webhook) vs Argo pre-merge policy check. We propose a layered approach: verify at PR time + cluster admission for defense in depth.

Helm chart and GitOps layout notes:
- Chart versioning: keep charts semver independent of images. Use image.tag in values.yaml and prefer digest pinned fields (image.digest) for production releases.
- GitOps repo structure: apps/<env>/<app>/values.yaml. Use templates so PR updates only keys under values.image: { registry, repository, tag, digest }.
- Use Chart.lock or a generated release manifest when performing a release to ensure deterministic deploys.

Image tagging and signature policy:
- Tag scheme: <iso-date>-<channel>-sha<shortsha> e.g. 2025-11-04-prod-sha1234. Include channel (canary, prod).
- Always publish immutable digest-based references in the gitops repo: image: repo@sha256:<digest>. The CI should write digest after push/sign-step.
- Signatures: cosign attached to OCI artifact + attestation containing build metadata (CI run id, git sha, builder user).

KMS / key rotation playbook (sketch):
- Goal: rotate signing keys without causing existing deployed images' signature validations to break and with minimal downtime.
- Constraints: Admission controller / verification policy must accept signatures from either the old key or the new key for a bounded transition window.
- Steps:
  1) Provision new key in customer KMS via terraform module (see notes below) and grant Redwood signing principal encrypt/decrypt / sign privileges for that key only.
  2) Update cosign key references in CI secrets to point to new KMS key id (do not delete old reference).
  3) Start dual-signing: CI signs newly built images with both old and new key (cosign supports multiple signatures/attestations). Push both signatures.
  4) Update admission verification policy to accept either key (add new key fingerprint to allowed list). This should be coordinated with SRE/security.
  5) After X days (monitor: no blocked deploys), retire old key by removing it from policy and deleting from KMS following org key deletion policy.
  6) Update terraform to remove old key references as part of cleanup change.
- Emergency rollback: if new key misbehaves (e.g., not accepted by admission controller), revert CI secrets to old key and halt automated signing for new key until fix.

Terraform module notes (quick):
- Module: redwood_kms_signer (name: rw_kms_signer)
  - Inputs: key_alias, key_usage (SIGN_VERIFY), key_policy_json (optional), rotation_enabled (bool), tags
  - Outputs: key_id, key_arn, key_fingerprint
  - Recommended IAM bindings: allow cosign-role to sign only; do not give wide decrypt permissions. Use KMS:Sign / GetPublicKey as minimal surface.
- Module: registry_permissions
  - Inputs: registry_id, service_account_principal, push_permissions (bool), attestation_bucket (optional)
  - Outputs: registry_url, principal_id
- Upstreams: include module versions in the infra repo (pin to semver). Keep backward-compatible state migration notes in module CHANGELOG.

Upgrade/canary strategy (detailed):
- Canary size: 5% of pods or single node replica depending on topology. For stateful or multi-node apps, prefer node-anchored canary.
- Phases:
  1) dry-run manifest apply via argocd app diff (auto-generated) -> ensure no chart errors.
  2) pre-sync hooks: create canary deployment with label canary=true; set traffic routing (ingress/service mesh split) to route small portion of traffic.
  3) verification window: 10-20m baseline; collect metrics via Redwood observability hooks or external test runner.
  4) if metrics stable, update values to final replicas and remove canary label (promote).
  5) if failure, Argo rollback to previous commit; run failure postmortem template.
- Automations: Argo AppRollouts or Flagger can orchestrate traffic shifting; prefer Flagger for more complex feature sets but weigh operator footprint.

Image signing verification in CI & policy checks:
- Pre-merge CI job: fetch image digest -> verify signature via cosign verify -key kms://... --attestation -> fail PR if verification fails.
- Argo pre-sync plugin: run image verification hook to prevent sync if image is unsigned or signature missing. Consider OPA gate to enforce allowed-keys list.

Rollback & emergency flow:
- If health checks fail post-sync, Argo rollback to previous commit (image digest pinned).
- If registry image is compromised, block tag at registry level and revert gitops to previous digest.
- Escalation: create incident in PagerDuty -> run playbook (link to incident runbook).

Operational playbook checklist (for release run):
- [ ] CI build green + artifacts stored + digest recorded
- [ ] Image signed and cosign attestation present
- [ ] PR opened updating gitops values with digest + release notes + signed-verify output
- [ ] Security gate checks (allowed registry, key fingerprint) passed
- [ ] Merge -> Argo sync queued -> canary hooks configured
- [ ] Canary smoke tests passed within window
- [ ] Full roll after monitoring window and metrics OK
- [ ] Post-release verification (synthetic checks + logs)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical owner of signing keys: customer vs Redwood-managed HSM. Security review pending (SEC-Q4-2025).
- Confirm admission controller implementation: kube admission webhook maintained by customer or Redwood-provided operator? Add conftest/OPA policy templates.
- Add terraform example code + small module README for rw_kms_signer (TODO: create PR in infra repo).
- Document key rotation SLOs and retention policy for old signatures.

Appendix: quick command cheatsheet (examples)
- Sign with cosign (KMS): cosign sign --key "kms://projects/PROJECT/locations/global/keyRings/RING/cryptoKeys/KEY/cryptoKeyVersions/1" docker.io/org/repo@sha256:abcd123
- Verify signature: cosign verify --key "kms://projects/.../cryptoKeys/KEY" docker.io/org/repo@sha256:abcd123
- Dual sign (old + new): cosign sign --key kms://old-key ... ; cosign sign --key kms://new-key ...
- Get digest after push: skopeo inspect --raw docker://registry/repo:tag | sha256sum (CI should capture and write digest to gitops repo)

Contacts / owners:
- Draft owner: Asha Patel (eng-private-deploy).
- Security reviewer: Priya Nair (security).
- Infra / Terraform: Diego Marin (platform infra).

Last notes:
This is intentionally pragmatic and contains operational tradeoffs. Next steps: schedule 1-hour working session with Security + Infra to lock key ownership and finalize admission policy; create infra PR for rw_kms_signer skeleton and CI change to dual-sign for next 2 weeks (PD-1987).
